params.body:
`storage/logs/laravel.log` on production stood at **2,330,128,131 bytes**: one
file, written since its first line on 10 May 2022. Nobody reads a file that
size, and the tail is the only part anyone ever wants.

The `stack` channel wrote to `single`. It now writes to `daily`, with `bugsnag`
next to it exactly as before: rotation is about the file on disk, not about where
an exception gets reported. `LOG_CHANNEL` is already `stack` on production, so
this arrives with the deploy and needs no change to the environment. Retention is
`LOG_DAILY_DAYS`, default 14, so it can be turned up per environment without
touching this file.

## Already done on the box

The old file has been moved aside, not deleted: it is
`storage/logs/laravel-2022-05-10-to-2026-09-18.log.gz` (four years of history,
compressed), and `laravel.log` starts empty. So the first rotation begins from
nothing rather than from 2,3 GB.

## What was in it, since the question comes up

About 60% of the sampled volume is one thing: a per-step trace of the Smartschool
OAuth flow, thirteen INFO lines per login ("redirect START", "Config loaded",
"Building provider", "Config set", "Redirect response created", and the same
again for the callback). Those log calls are not in `app/` any more and the last
one in the file is dated 9 September, so this is history, not a flood that is
still running. Today's growth was about 450 kB.
params.title: Het log rolt: daily in plaats van één bestand van 2,3 GB
